BE IT ORDAINED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, WYOMING:
Section 1.
That, pursuant to WYO. STAT.15-7-407 the Board of Public Utilities (BOARD) shal
fix the ratesfor water and sanitary sewer services furnished to customers, and anyrevision thereof is subject to
the governing body's review, modification and approval.
Section2.
That, pursuant to City Code Section 13.04.140, rates and charges for the consumption of
cityutility services, charges and fees for connections, inspections, penalties, shutoff enalties and meter
installations shall be established by theBOARD, approved by the Governing Body and filed with the City Clerk
and business office of the Board.
eachfiscal year the BOARD will calculate new rates forwater and sewer services based on the Bureau of Labor
Statistics, Consumer Price Index, All Urban Consumers, Water and Sewer Maintenance and the Wyoming Cost
Living Index-Southeast Region and prepare new rate schedules for Water and Sewer services; andwhereas, the
Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index, All Urban Consumers, Water and Sewer Maintenance for the
calendar year 2012was 6.7% and the Wyoming Cost Living Index-Southeast Region for the fourth quarter of
2012 was 3.4%;
Section4.That the BOARD established by Resolution No.2013-3, adopted May 01,2013,
revised water rates as shown and set forth on the resolution attached hereto as Exhibit A.
Section5.
That the BOARD established by Resolution No.2013-o4, adopted May01,2013,
revised sewer rates as shown and set forth on the resolution attached hereto as Exhibit B.
Section6.
That theBOARD established by Resolution No.2013-5, adopted May 01,2013,
revised Tap Fees, Water And Sewer System Development Fees, Pump Station And Related Fees as shown and set
forth on the resolution attached hereto as Exhibit C.
Section 7.That the BOARD established by Resolution No.2013-06, adopted May 01,2013,
revised Administrative fees, service charges and penalties as shown and set forth onthe resolution attached hereto
as Exhibit D.
Section 8.
That the BOARD established by Resolution No. 2013-O2_, adopted May 01,2013,
revised Septic Waste Dump Rates and Commercial Waste Rates as shown and set forth on the resolution attached
hereto as Exhibit E.
Section 9.
That the Governing Body has reviewed the rates, charges and fees established by the
BOARDfor water and sewer services and hereby approves the water and sewer rate schedules attached hereto.
Section 10.That prior to the beginning of eachfiscal year, the BOARDwill calculate new rates for
Water and Sewer services based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index, All Urban Consumers,
Water and Sewer Maintenance and the Wyoming Cost Living Index-Southeast Region and prepare newrate
schedules for Water and Sewer services that shall be presented, in the form of an ordinance, to the Governing
Body.
Section 11.
That this ordinance shall be in full force and effect upon its passage and publication.

WHEREAS, the Board of Public Utilities (Board)is authorized by State Statute and City Code to
set rates, fees and penalties for water and sanitary sewer services furnished to customers; and
(a)Pay for the operation and maintenance of the sanitary sewer system, including
salaries, wages and benefits, and the cost of all materials and supplies necessary for
repairs, replacements and upgrades to the system;
(b)Pay interest charges and principal payments on all outstanding sewer loans and bonds
as they are due;
(c) Cover all miscellaneous expenses;
(d) Cover all usual extensions and enlargements, together with a reasonable allowance
for emergency and unforeseen expenses; and
(e)Provide and maintain a depreciation fund for the sewer department;
WHEREAS, the Board has determined that an increase in the Septic Waste Dump and
Commercial Waste rates are necessary to ensure adequate revenue is generated in order to payfor costs
associated with those services rendered;

and Sewer Maintenance for the calendar year 2012was 6.7% and the Wyoming Cost of Living Index --
Southeast Region for the fourth quarter of 2012was 3.4%.

of 2012 of 3.4%.
